body.p: Claims 1-46 are currently pending in the application. Claims 1-46 were rejected in the Office Action mailed August 14, 2024 (hereinafter referred to as "Office Action").

Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that this paper is being filed with all required fees. However, if an additional fee is due, including those for an extension of time please charge any fees required or credit any overpayment to Chalker Flores, LLP's Deposit Account No. 50-4863 during the pendency of this application pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 1.16 through 1.21 inclusive, and any other section in Title 37 of the Code of Federal Regulations that may regulate fees. If an extension of time is required with this response but is not included, applicant(s) hereby petition(s) for a Request for Extension of Time under 37 C.F.R. § 1.136(a).
In view of the following remarks and amendments, Applicant(s) respectfully request(s) a timely Notice of Allowance be issued in this case.

The Office Action rejected claims 1-3, 7, 9-10, 16, 19, 23, 25- 26 & 32, 35, 39, 41 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Fisher et al., Pub. No.: US 20160229547 Al (hereinafter "Fisher"), in view of Barnes et al., Pub. No.: US 20070118254 Al (hereinafter "Barnes"). The Office Action rejected claims 4-6, 20-22 & 36-38 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Fisher, in view of Barnes, further in view of Elfeky et al., Pub. No.: US 20170217584 Al (hereinafter "Elfeky"). The Office Action rejected claims 15, 27, 31, 43 & 46 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Fisher, in view of Barnes, further in view of Elfeky. The Office Action rejected claims 8, 24 & 40 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Fisher, in view of Barnes, further in view of Weinhofer et al., Pub. No.: US 20050067995 Al (hereinafter "Weinhofer"). The Office Action rejected claims 11, 28 & 44 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Fisher, in view of Barnes, further in view of

Cherepinsky et al., Pub. No.: US 20080283671 Al (hereinafter "Cherepinsky"). The Office Action rejected claims 12-13, 29-30, 42 & 45 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Fisher, in view of Barnes, further in view of McClelland et al., Pub. No.: US 20020125852 Al (hereinafter "McClelland"). The Office Action rejected claims 14, 17-18 and 33-34 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Fisher, in view of Barnes, further in view of Irwin '811,
Patent No.: US 4071811 A (hereinafter "Irwin").

Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that claims 1-46 are allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 103 for at least the reasons set forth below. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are respectfully requested.
Claims 1, 16 and 32
Without conceding the correctness of the rejections in the Office Action, claims 1, 16 and 32 have been amended to change "rotor system" to "rotor assembly", and "moving the rotor

system from a first position" to "moving the rotor assembly or a pylon thereof from a first position." Support for the amendments can be found in paragraph [0030] ("Tilt rotor assemblies 1 02a and 1 02b move or rotate"), paragraph [0031] ("pylons 210Oa and 210Ob with the rotor assemblies 202a and 202b rotate to redirect the thrust from the rotor assemblies 202a and 202b") and FIGS. 1A-2B.

In addition, the Office Action equated the "rotor system" recited in claims 1, 16 and 32 to the "rotor speed control 12" of Barnes. (page 3). Similarly, the Office Action equated the "rotor system" recited in claims 1, 16 and 32 to the "power control lever 30" of Fisher. (page 4). Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that the "rotor assembly or pylon thereof ' as recited in claims 1, 16 and 32, as amended, is not a "rotor speed control" or a "power control lever" because the specification identifies the rotor assembly as elements 102a, 102b in FIGS. lA-1B, and pylons as elements 210a, 210b of rotor assembly 202a, 202b in FIGS. 2A-2B.

For at least the foregoing reasons, applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that Fisher and Barnes, either alone or in combination, do not disclose, teach or suggest each and every element of claims 1, 16 and 32. Claims 1, 16 and 32 are, therefore, allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 103. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are respectfully requested.

Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that the deficiencies detailed above in reference to the cited references are sufficient to traverse the rejections. As a result, any additional distinctions between the claims and the cited references are unnecessary and applicant(s) reserve(s) the right to present additional arguments against the statements and characterizations stated in the Office Action, and the cited reference in the event the rejections are not withdrawn.
Claims 2-3, 19 and 35

Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that claims 2-3, 19 and 20 are allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 103 because they directly or indirectly depend from claims 1, 16 and 32, which are allowable for at least the reasons set forth above. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are respectfully requested.

In addition, the Office Action equated the "rotor system" recited in claims 2-3, 19 and 35 to the "power control lever 30" of Fisher. (pages 4-5). Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that the "rotor assembly or pylon thereof' as recited in claims 2-3, 19 and 35, as amended, is not a "rotor speed control" or a "power control lever" because the specification identifies the rotor assembly as elements 102a, 102b in FIGS. lA-1B, and pylons as elements 210a, 210b of rotor assembly 202a, 202b in FIGS. 2A-2B.

For at least the foregoing reasons, applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that Fisher and Barnes, either alone or in combination, do not disclose, teach or suggest each and every element of claims 2-3, 19 and 35. Claims 2-3, 19 and 35 are, therefore, allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 103. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are respectfully requested.

Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that the deficiencies detailed above in reference to the cited references are sufficient to traverse the rejections. As a result, any additional distinctions between the claims and the cited references are unnecessary and applicant(s) reserve(s) the right to present additional arguments against the statements and characterizations stated in the Office Action, and the cited reference in the event the rejections are not withdrawn.

Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that claims 4-15, 17-18, 20-31, 33-34 and 36-46 are allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 103 because they directly or indirectly depend from claims 1, 16 and 32, which are allowable for at least the reasons set forth above. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are respectfully requested.

Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that the deficiencies detailed above in reference to the cited references are sufficient to traverse the rejections. As a result, any additional distinctions between the claims and the cited references are unnecessary and applicant(s) reserve(s) the right to present additional arguments against the statements and characterizations stated in the Office Action, and the cited reference in the event the rejections are not withdrawn.
The Office Action rejected claims 1, 16 and 32 on the grounds of nonstatutory obviousness-type double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 1, 15 and 27 of U.S. Patent No. 11,072,434.
Applicant(s) will file a terminal disclaimer upon allowance of the claims if the terminal disclaimer is still necessary.

For the reasons set forth above, Applicant(s) respectfully request(s) reconsideration by the examiner and withdrawal of the rejections. Applicant(s) submit(s) that claims 1-46 are fully patentable. Applicant(s) respectfully request(s) that a timely Notice of Allowance be issued in this case.
